_note: The 9-week timetable. Week titles, summaries, daily activities, AI notes and tools come from barcelonacodeschool.com/ux-design-bootcamp-in-barcelona-code-school/. The daily routine, Figma/Framer workshops and Check Points come from the Notion 'UX Day by Day' board. A tag's 'link' is a page on this site (section/slug).

standup.title: Daily Stand Up
standup.text: Morning scrum that gives focus for the day ahead.

checkout.title: Daily Check Out
checkout.text: Evening scrum that gives closure for the day past.

weeks.summary: A two-week service design sprint. Go out into the real world, map how a service actually behaves today, and build the evidence base for redesigning it.
weeks.ai: Claude for desk research synthesis and benchmarking matrices; multimodal inspiration loops for moodboarding.

weeks.summary: A startup business and design sprint that goes beyond UX into high-level market decisions. Learn to argue for a design in the language a business actually uses.
weeks.ai: Structured prompting to pressure-test assumptions, generate survey drafts you then edit as a researcher, and cluster open-ended responses.

activities.label: Lean UX Canvas built with Claude

weeks.summary: Back to week one's service design sprint, ending by putting your design decisions in front of real prospective users – in public, not in a classroom.
weeks.ai: Prompt-to-prototype for mid-fidelity screens, then AI-assisted synthesis of testing notes into themes you verify against the raw data.

weeks.summary: Back to the startup project to work out the core purpose and functionality of an app. Know what your users need – and, harder, what they don't.
weeks.ai: Design-system-aware generation, AI affinity clustering, and Desirability–Viability–Feasibility analysis with an AI sparring partner.

weeks.summary: A full week to turn two finished sprints into written case studies – the week most bootcamps skip, and the reason most junior portfolios never get read past the first screen.
weeks.ai: Using AI as an editor and critic, not a ghostwriter. Quality rubrics that keep your voice and kill generic AI-written filler.

activities.label: Service design and lean startup projects
Synthesising and cataloguing artifacts from all prior projects

weeks.summary: A high-stakes challenge with no clean answer. Using Claude Code and Claude Design, deep-dive into design thinking as a method for tackling genuinely messy, systemic problems.
weeks.ai: Claude Code and Claude Design for building working concept prototypes in hours instead of weeks; context engineering for long, complex research threads.

days.presentation: Solution pitch and concept design review

weeks.summary: A two-week personal project – your first chance to develop and defend your own UX methodology. Choose the topic: something entirely your own, or a continuation of an earlier sprint.
weeks.ai: Building your own reusable AI workflow – Claude.md and Skill.md project files so the model knows your product, your users and your standards.

weeks.summary: The second half of the personal project: from paper to a high-fidelity, tested product, with the before-and-after evidence that hiring managers ask for.
weeks.ai: Automated verification and LLM-as-a-judge testing loops to catch accessibility, consistency and content errors before your users do.

weeks.summary: Use the latest AI tools to build and ship your own portfolio website. Leave with skills, theory, case studies and a live portfolio – ready to start applying.
weeks.ai: Shipping a real, hosted site with Framer AI or Claude Code – plus how to talk about your AI workflow in an interview without sounding like you outsourced your thinking.

activities.label: Website development with Framer AI, or Claude Code with GitHub and React.js
